## Root cause

The warning is a **stale, un-refcounted `struct device *` cached in `struct typec_port`** being handed to `sysfs_remove_link()` after the target device's sysfs directory has already been torn down.

### 1. Where the WARN comes from

`linux/fs/kernfs/dir.c:1724-1734`:

```c
int kernfs_remove_by_name_ns(struct kernfs_node *parent, const char *name, ...)
{
	if (!parent) {
		WARN(1, KERN_WARNING "kernfs: can not remove '%s', no directory\n", name);
		return -ENOENT;
	}
```

So `parent == NULL`. `parent` comes from `kobj->sd`:

- `linux/fs/sysfs/symlink.c:143-153` — `sysfs_remove_link()` → `parent = kobj->sd; kernfs_remove_by_name(parent, name)`.
- `kobj->sd` is NULLed when the kobject's directory is removed: `linux/fs/sysfs/dir.c:95-97` (`sysfs_remove_dir()`: `spin_lock(&sysfs_symlink_target_lock); kobj->sd = NULL;`).

⇒ The link named `"typec"` is being removed from a **kobject whose sysfs dir is already gone** (device already went through `device_del()`), hence ENOENT/`no directory`.

### 2. The offending function: `typec_partner_unlink_device()`

`linux/drivers/usb/typec/class.c:906-913`:

```c
static void typec_partner_unlink_device(struct typec_partner *partner, struct device *dev)
{
	sysfs_remove_link(&partner->dev.kobj, dev_name(dev));
	sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");	/* <-- line 909: dev->kobj.sd == NULL */
	...
}
```

`"typec"` is the exact link name in the WARN string. Created symmetrically at `class.c:892`.

Callers, both in the reported chain:

- `linux/drivers/usb/typec/class.c:1174-1195` `typec_unregister_partner()`:
  ```c
  mutex_lock(&port->partner_link_lock);
  if (port->usb2_dev) { typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb2_dev); port->usb2_dev = NULL; }  /* :1184-1187 */
  if (port->usb3_dev) { typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb3_dev); port->usb3_dev = NULL; }  /* :1188-1191 */
  device_unregister(&partner->dev);
  ```
- `class.c:2169-2186` `typec_partner_deattach()` (the `con->deattach` callback, installed at `class.c:2753`).

### 3. Why `port->usb2_dev` / `port->usb3_dev` is stale

The cached pointers are declared with an explicit REVISIT comment at `linux/drivers/usb/typec/class.h:77-85`:

```c
	/* REVISIT: Only USB devices for now. ...
	 * NOTE: These may be registered first before the typec_partner, so they
	 * will always have to be kept here instead of struct typec_partner. */
	struct device *usb2_dev;   /* class.h:84 */
	struct device *usb3_dev;   /* class.h:85 */
```

They are stored **without `get_device()`** — `typec_partner_attach()` at `class.c:2144-2166`:

```c
	if (udev->speed < USB_SPEED_SUPER) { usb_mode = USB_MODE_USB2; port->usb2_dev = dev; }  /* :2153-2154 */
	else                               { usb_mode = USB_MODE_USB3; port->usb3_dev = dev; }  /* :2156-2157 */
```

(`grep get_device linux/drivers/usb/typec/class.c` → only `class.c:681`, for altmode parents; nothing for `usb2_dev`/`usb3_dev`.)

The only thing that clears them on the USB side is the deattach callback, which is reached exclusively through `port_dev->connector`:

- `linux/include/linux/usb/typec.h:410-414` — `typec_deattach()` is a **no-op if `con == NULL`**.
- `linux/drivers/usb/core/hub.c:2363` — `usb_disconnect()`: `typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, &udev->dev);` (before `device_del(&udev->dev)` at `hub.c:2376`, so this path is fine).
- **Asymmetry / the actual leak** — `linux/drivers/usb/core/port.c:722-729`:
  ```c
  static void connector_unbind(struct device *dev, struct device *connector, void *data)
  {
	sysfs_remove_link(&connector->kobj, dev_name(dev));
	sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "connector");
	port_dev->connector = NULL;		/* port.c:728 — no typec_deattach()! */
  }
  ```
  compare the bind side, which *does* attach an already-enumerated child: `port.c:710-717` (`port_dev->connector = data; if (port_dev->child) typec_attach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);`).

So once the component master is torn down (`typec_unregister_port()` → `typec_unlink_ports()`, `class.c:2828-2835`; `port-mapper.c:102-106` → `component_master_del()` → `connector_unbind`, registered at `port.c:731-734`, `component_add` at `port.c:789` / `component_del` at `port.c:846`), the Type‑C port keeps `usb2_dev`/`usb3_dev` pointing at the USB device, while `port_dev->connector` is NULL — so the later `usb_disconnect()` silently skips `typec_deattach()` (`hub.c:2363`), `device_del()` runs (`hub.c:2376` → `sysfs_remove_dir()` → `kobj->sd = NULL`), and the pointer becomes stale.

### 4. The boot-time chain on this machine

1. Dock/retimer USB devices are already enumerated when UCSI (ACPI PPM) probes; `typec_link_ports()` (`class.c:2814`) binds the components → `connector_bind()` → `typec_attach()` → `port->usb2_dev`/`usb3_dev` cached (`class.c:2154`/`:2157`).
2. Any port/component teardown or re-probe (`ucsi_init` error path `ucsi.c:1909-1926`, or `ucsi_unregister()` `ucsi.c:2144-2150`, both calling `ucsi_unregister_partner()` then `typec_unregister_port()`) runs `connector_unbind()` → `port_dev->connector = NULL` **without** deattach.
3. The USB device disconnects; `typec_deattach()` is a no-op; `udev->dev.kobj.sd = NULL`.
4. BIOS sends a connector-change notification → `ucsi_connector_change()` (`ucsi.c:1372-1385`) → `schedule_work(&con->work)` = `ucsi_handle_connector_change()` (`ucsi.c:1264`, registered `ucsi.c:1632`), i.e. `kworker/6:0` / `events`.
5. `change & UCSI_CONSTAT_CONNECT_CHANGE` with `!UCSI_CONSTAT(con, CONNECTED)` → `ucsi_unregister_partner(con)` (`ucsi.c:1325`; same at `ucsi.c:1221` from `ucsi_check_connection()`).
6. `ucsi_unregister_partner()` (`ucsi.c:1138-1154`) → `typec_unregister_partner(con->partner)` (`ucsi.c:1151`).
7. `typec_unregister_partner()` (`class.c:1184-1189`) → `typec_partner_unlink_device()` → `sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec")` (`class.c:909`) → `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()` with `parent == NULL` → **WARN at fs/kernfs/dir.c:1731** (matches your `dir.c:1706` on 6.17; line numbers shifted in this tree).

Exactly matches the reported stack: `ucsi_handle_connector_change → ucsi_unregister_partner → typec_unregister_partner → kernfs_remove_by_name_ns`.

## Minimal fix (two parts)

1. `linux/drivers/usb/core/port.c:722` — make unbind symmetric with `connector_bind()`:
```c
static void connector_unbind(struct device *dev, struct device *connector, void *data)
{
	struct usb_port *port_dev = to_usb_port(dev);

	if (port_dev->child)
		typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);
	sysfs_remove_link(&connector->kobj, dev_name(dev));
	sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "connector");
	port_dev->connector = NULL;
}
```
2. `linux/drivers/usb/typec/class.c` — refcount the cached devices: `get_device(dev)` at `:2154`/`:2157` (and in `typec_register_partner()`'s use at `:1158-1161`), `put_device()` where they are cleared at `:1186`, `:1190`, `:2182-2184`. This turns the remaining window into a harmless removal of an already-removed link instead of a WARN/potential use-after-free.

The WARN itself is benign (ENOENT is returned, nothing is corrupted), but it is a genuine dangling-pointer indicator — with a slightly different timing the same pointer is dereferenced in `dev_name(dev)` at `class.c:908` on freed memory.
